meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Cook Islands (self-governing state in free association with New Zealand; Realm of New Zealand)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — English common law foundation overlaid by the Cook Islands International Companies Act 1981-82 (as amended); local statutory company and AML/CFT regimes; self-governing territory exercising home rule, with New Zealand retaining responsibility for external affairs and nationality

Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (PACER Plus, 2017)
Agreement between New Zealand and the Cook Islands for the Exchange of Information with Respect to Taxes (TIEA, 2009)
Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards, New York 1958 (extended to the Cook Islands by New Zealand)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Cook Islands International Companies Act 1981-82 (as amended), ss 25-30 (company names), ss 62-84 (registered office, agent, constitution); Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism Act 2018, Parts 2 and 3 (customer due diligence, beneficial ownership, reporting obligations); Financial Supervisory Commission Act 2003; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2018; AML/CFT Rules 2019 issued by the Financial Supervisory Commission; Beneficial Ownership (Prescribed Exemptions) Regulations 2019

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the individual's country of origin or resident country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention extended to the Cook Islands via New Zealand's territorial application) OR full consular legalization if originating from a non-Apostille state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address — utility bill, bank statement, or government-issued certificate dated within 3 months
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, licensed bank, or public registry of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille OR consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / professional reference letter from a licensed financial institution or chartered accountant
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or licensed public accountant in the applicant's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Direct issuance to the Cook Islands licensed agent (no apostille required where issued by regulated institution); apostille recommended for non-regulated originators

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency or extracts from any existing corporate vehicle in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or registered agent of the existing entity's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization of the original certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (if a corporate service provider acts for the incorporators)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of execution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory electronic screening of all Directors, Shareholders, and UBOs against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, EU Consolidated List, and Cook Islands domestic sanctions designations; Enhanced Due Diligence required for Domestic and Foreign Politically Exposed Persons under the AML/CFT Act 2018 and FATF Recommendations 12 and 22; continuous transaction monitoring and 5-year client relationship risk re-assessment mandated by AML/CFT Rules 2019; screening records retained for at least 6 years post business relationship termination.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission — International Companies Registration System (online portal at www.fsc.gov.ck)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be rendered in the Latin alphabet; names in non-Latin scripts are not accepted unless transliterated into English with a certified translation filed with the Registrar; Cook Islands Māori and English names are permissible using standard Latin characters; the name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any existing registered international company, foreign company, or reserved name; the name must end with 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc.', 'Pty Ltd', or equivalent acceptable suffix.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon notification of name rejection, the applicant (through the licensed agent) may file a written request for reconsideration with the Registrar of International Companies within 14 days of the rejection notice, stating grounds of non-confusion and attaching consent letters or trade-mark evidence where applicable. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may submit a formal administrative review application to the Financial Supervisory Commission within a further 14 days, which the Commission shall determine within 28 days of filing. If the Commission affirms the refusal, the applicant may institute judicial review proceedings in the High Court of the Cook Islands under the Judicature Act 1980-81 within 30 days of the Commission's decision, with leave of the Court. All appeal steps must be channelled through the licensed Cook Islands registered agent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office does not satisfy the statutory requirement of a physical registered office located in the Cook Islands; the registered office must be the physical premises of a licensed international company agent or registered office provider in Rarotonga. Fully remote operational premises for e-commerce retail (server locations, drop-shipping warehouses, and management functions) are permissible and will not disturb the tax-exempt international company status, provided the company does not trade within the Cook Islands domestic market.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate — approximately 40-55% likelihood of an unannounced FSC on-site inspection at the licensed agent's registered office within the first 12 months of incorporation as part of AML/CFT supervisory inspection cycles; direct physical inspection of the company's remote operational premises outside the Cook Islands is not conducted by the FSC.

incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies / International Companies Unit, Companies Office, New Zealand Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), 15 Stout Street, Wellington; online portal: https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Companies Act 1993 Form 1 - Application for Incorporation of a Company; for International Company status, the International Companies Act 1974 registration application and agent's certificate in the form prescribed by the Registrar.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum paid-up capital applies under the Companies Act 1993 (ss 46-47). Capital may be nominal, but a paid-up sum of at least NZ$100 is recommended for commercial bank account acceptance. No escrow account is mandatory for incorporation; if paid-up capital is held in escrow, it must be placed in a bank account with a New Zealand registered bank and documented in the share subscription agreement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLVED, effective immediately upon registration: 

1. The incorporation application, the Constitution, and the registered office details as tabled are approved and adopted. 

2. The Board accepts the allotment of 1,000 ordinary shares of NZ$0.10 each, being paid-up capital of NZ$100, to the founding subscriber(s) as consideration for the business assets or cash contributed, and directs that share certificates be issued to each shareholder. 

3. The registered office of the Company is fixed at [address], New Zealand, and the address for service is recorded with the Registrar. 

4. The directors named in the consent certificates are appointed as the first Board of Directors. [Name] is appointed Chief Executive and [Name] is appointed Company Secretary and AML Compliance Officer. 

5. The Board is authorised to retain the registered agent, open bank accounts, engage external professional advisers, and take all procedural steps necessary to complete statutory incorporation and licensing or compliance obligations. 

6. Any one director or the Company Secretary is authorised to execute all applications, consents, and ancillary instruments and to affix the common seal if adopted. 

All resolutions to be effective nunc pro tunc as of registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Entity Type Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office; online name reservation portal through RealMe at https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name availability search and submit the prescribed Name Reservation application. Confirm that the proposed company name, including any International Company designation, complies with s 22 of the Companies Act 1993 and the restricted-name provisions of the Companies (Restricted Names) Regulations. If the name contains a restricted word or phrase, obtain the prior written consent of the relevant MBIE sector regulator and attach it to the application. For an International Company, confirm with the International Companies Unit that the entity will be established solely for lawful offshore or exempt activity and that the registered agent is accepted.
required_dossiers: Proposed name and entity type selection
Written consent from restricted-name regulator (if applicable)
Director and shareholder identity verification pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, file a revised name reservation with a differentiated name within 10 working days, or request written reasons from the Registrar. If the Registrar refuses under s 23, the applicant may submit an alternative name without additional statutory fee and, if still aggrieved, apply for judicial review in the High Court after exhausting the administrative re-submission route.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Constitution and Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company's legal counsel and corporate services provider; final documents submitted to the Companies Office as part of the incorporation application
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Constitution in accordance with s 24 of the Companies Act 1993, covering share classes, director powers, quorum, voting, indemnity, and distribution rules. Prepare the share subscription agreement, first directors' consents, registered office consent, and address for service instrument. Ensure all subscribers and directors execute the documents in wet-ink or with a qualified electronic signature. If no constitution is adopted, the default constitution, comprising the applicable provisions of the Companies Act 1993, applies automatically; for an International Company, adopt the supplemental governance clauses required by the International Companies Act 1974, including non-resident ownership recognition and exempt-status undertakings.
required_dossiers: Signed Constitution or election to use the statutory default constitution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Office queries any constitutional provision for inconsistency with the Companies Act 1993, convene a subscriber meeting, amend the Constitution by written resolution, re-execute it, and resubmit. Corrections may be made voluntarily before registration; after registration, a special resolution under s 117 is required to alter the constitution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of State Fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, MBIE; online submission through the Companies Office incorporation interface
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and lodge the incorporation application with the prescribed particulars of the company name, registered office, address for service, directors, shareholders, initial share structure, and constitution election. Attach all director consents and registered office consents. Declare that the company is not carrying on a prohibited business and that all information is true and complete. Pay the official filing fee by credit card or online banking. For an International Company, ensure the covering registered agent certificate is included and that the International Companies Unit has pre-approved the agent.
required_dossiers: Registered office and address for service forms
Share allotment schedule with subscriber details
Registered agent certificate and AML due-diligence pack
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or notice of proposed refusal under ss 13-14, respond in writing within the specified period, ordinarily 10 working days, with corrected particulars or supporting declarations. If the Registrar still refuses, request a refund of the filing fee, less an administrative deduction, and restart with a corrected application; a refusal may also be appealed to the High Court under the Judicature Amendment Act 1972.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN Allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office; New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, obtain the Certificate of Incorporation electronically from the Companies Register. Verify that the company name, company number, date of incorporation, registered office, and directors are correctly recorded. Download the official company extract and NZBN allocation. For International Company status, retain the certificate issued under the International Companies Act 1974 and the Registrar's confirmation of exempt or non-resident classification.
required_dossiers: Paying-in record of state filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a clerical or legal error, apply to the Registrar under s 205 to correct the Companies Register, providing a statutory declaration and supporting evidence. If correction is refused, the company or an aggrieved party may apply to the High Court for an order directing rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirmation of Registered Office and Resident Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Companies Office; International Companies Unit for international company registered agents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the registered office is a physical address in New Zealand that is not solely a post-office box; the office must be open to the public during normal business hours. File the registered office consent and record any change of address using the Companies Office address-change process. For an International Company, execute the registered agent agreement, confirm the agent's eligibility, and file the agent's certificate with the Companies Office within 10 working days of any change.
required_dossiers: Registered office consent and physical address proof
Notice of change of registered office, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office is rejected because it fails the physical-access requirement, secure an alternative compliant office, obtain a fresh consent letter, and file an address-change notice immediately. If the Registrar issues a notice that the registered office is no longer effective, remedy the filing within 10 working days to avoid compulsory striking-off under s 318.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake), Wellington, New Zealand; online portal: myIR Secure Online Services (https://www.ird.govt.nz). Corporate registration and tax identity issuance are coordinated with the New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment) and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) registry (https://www.nzbn.govt.nz).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 — Incorporation: register the CK_IC International Company with the New Zealand Companies Office via the online Companies Register; the NZBN is issued automatically. Step 2 — IRD number: apply for the entity's Inland Revenue Department number either through the incorporation application checklist or via myIR / paper form IR596 (Application for an IRD Number – Non-Individual); this is mandatory before the entity can file returns, pay tax, or register for GST. Step 3 — GST registration: once taxable supplies exceed, or are expected to exceed, NZ$60,000 in a rolling 12-month period, submit GST101 (GST registration, cancellation, and change of details) through myIR; voluntary registration under s 51 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 is available below the threshold. Step 4 — NRWT registration: register for non-resident withholding tax obligations if the entity derives or pays New Zealand-source dividends, interest, or royalties. Step 5 — Fully foreign-owned offshore companies: a non-resident company with a New Zealand presence (place of business, branch, or fixed establishment) must first register as an overseas company under Part 18 of the Companies Act 1993, obtain an NZBN, apply for an IRD number, and then assess mandatory GST registration under the same NZ$60,000 threshold. A non-resident entity with no New Zealand taxable nexus is not required to register; New Zealand withholding obligations are instead enforced against the New Zealand resident payer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone (custom CK_IC 'International Company' pipeline designation). In New Zealand statutory terms the default position is Entity_Level_Taxation combined with Territorial_Scope: an NZ-incorporated company is tax resident and is liable at the 28% corporate rate on world-wide income, whereas a non-resident company without a permanent establishment in New Zealand is chargeable only on New Zealand-source income. The resident entity's exposure to foreign active business income is, however, substantially neutralised by the CFC active-income exemption (Income Tax Act 2007, subpart EX) and the foreign dividend exemption (Income Tax Act 2007, s CW 9). The Tax_Exempt_Zone flag therefore denotes a ring-fenced offshore vehicle model with no New Zealand resident tax nexus and no physical economic presence in New Zealand, rather than a statutory free-trade or tax-free zone; New Zealand does not maintain legislated tax-exempt commercial zones.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: 1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007 (form IR879): an NZ-incorporated close company with five or fewer eligible shareholders may elect full fiscal transparency, with income, expenditure, losses, and tax credits attributed to shareholders, analogous in effect to a US check-the-box election. 2) Qualifying Company (QC) election: grandfathered regime; no new qualifying company elections have been permitted since 30 March 2011. 3) Consolidated group election under subpart FM of the Income Tax Act 2007: wholly owned NZ-resident corporate groups may elect to file a single consolidated return. 4) GST elections: taxable period election (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly under s 15 of the GST Act 1985); accounting basis election between payments/cash basis and invoice/accrual basis under ss 19–20 of the GST Act 1985; margin scheme election for second-hand goods under s 60D; and the zero-rating election for supplies of land between GST-registered persons under s 11(1)(mb). 5) Hybrid mismatch rules (Part 4B of the Income Tax Act 2007): wholly mandatory; no elective mechanism exists — structured arrangements exploiting entity classification differences are statutorily recharacterised to deny deductions or enforce income inclusions. 6) Transfer pricing: mandatory arm's length standard, with voluntary Advance Pricing Agreements (APAs) available from the IRD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — broad-based, consumption-type value added tax (Goods and Services Tax Act 1985)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 — compulsory registration applies once taxable supplies made in New Zealand exceed, or are expected to exceed, NZ$60,000 in a rolling 12-month period (s 51, GST Act 1985); voluntary registration is available below the threshold. Special nexus: non-resident suppliers of remote services (including digital products) and of low-value imported goods (goods valued at or below NZ$1,000 at the time of import) must register for GST when their supplies to New Zealand resident consumers exceed NZ$60,000 in a 12-month period; no physical presence in New Zealand is required to create this indirect tax nexus.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction controls (CTC), no government API pre-clearance, and no digital stamping mandate apply in New Zealand. E-invoicing is voluntary for the private sector and operates on the PEPPOL framework through the NZ e-Invoicing network; the New Zealand Government has a phased mandate requiring its own suppliers to issue e-invoices, but non-government businesses remain free to issue paper or PDF tax invoices. GST-registered persons must file returns electronically through myIR (GST101A or GST101B); paper filing is accepted only under limited IRD discretion. Tax invoices must contain the prescribed particulars in s 24 of the GST Act 1985: supplier name and GST number, date of issue, description of goods or services, quantity, price, and, for supplies over NZ$1,000, the buyer's name and address. The IRD does not operate a mandatory fiscal-stamping or invoice-clearance API for B2B or B2C transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: a supply is zero-rated under s 11(1)(a) of the GST Act 1985 where the supplier exports, or causes to be exported, the goods from New Zealand within 28 days after the time of supply and retains satisfactory evidence of export. The time of supply is normally the earlier of invoice issuance, payment receipt, or delivery/collection under s 9 of the GST Act 1985. The supplier must be responsible for the physical export; a sale where the foreign customer personally carries or ships the goods does not qualify for zero-rating. For the retail IoT hardware trade, goods delivered to a New Zealand address attract GST at 15%; export orders shipped by the seller via air or sea freight with Customs export declarations and transport documentation are zero-rated at 0%. Services: a supply of services is zero-rated under s 11A(1)(a) where the services are supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, unless the services are supplied in connection with land in New Zealand, goods located in New Zealand at the time of supply, or tangible personal property physically performed in New Zealand. Remote software, cloud, and post-sale support services for IoT devices supplied to offshore non-resident customers therefore qualify for zero-rating, provided the supplier holds contemporaneous evidence of the customer's non-resident status and off-shore location.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: New Zealand Customs Service electronic Export Declaration accepted in the Trade Single Window (Tradelink) — the statutory Customs export entry evidencing physical departure of the goods from New Zealand
Bill of Lading (sea freight) or Air Waybill (air freight) naming the CK_IC entity as shipper and the foreign buyer as consignee, evidencing export out of New Zealand
Commercial invoice (supplier copy) stating the HS tariff classification, quantity, unit price, Incoterms, and total export value
Packing list and carrier-generated delivery or booking documentation (terminal receipt, dock receipt, or courier manifest)
Inward Remittance Certificate, bank SWIFT credit advice, or other payment settlement evidence demonstrating receipt of the export sale proceeds from the overseas buyer
Certificate of Origin or Free Trade Agreement (FTA) certificate where a preferential tariff preference is claimed at the destination market
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: New Zealand does not statutorily impose a fixed 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline; the 180-day parameter is a pipeline default. The operative compliance framework is nonetheless strict: (i) if the exported goods leave New Zealand later than 28 days after the time of supply, the zero-rating fails and the supply is taxable at 15%, with the IRD issuing a default assessment for the unaccounted output tax (s 11 and s 24, GST Act 1985); (ii) the IRD may recharacterise unrepatriated export proceeds under the transfer pricing rules (Part 4A and s GC 6 et seq of the Income Tax Act 2007) where the sale price or settlement terms are not arm's length; (iii) the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG 1) and the specific GST avoidance provision (s 76 of the GST Act 1985) permit retrospective clawback of the zero-rated treatment where a GST advantage is the dominant purpose of the arrangement. Administrative consequences include shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994: 20% for lack of reasonable care (s 141A), unacceptable tax position (s 141B), or substantial understatement (s 141EB); 40% for gross carelessness (s 141C); 100% for an abusive tax position (s 141D); and 150% for evasion (s 141E). Use-of-money interest applies under Part 7 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 on any resulting underpayment. Criminal liability may arise under ss 143A–143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, with fines of up to NZ$50,000 for evasion (plus daily penalties for continuing offences) and imprisonment available for serious fraud. Records supporting export zero-rating must be retained for at least seven years under s 22 of the Tax Administration Act 1994. In addition, inaccurate export declarations expose the exporter to penalties and prosecution under the Customs and Excise Act 2018, including seizure of the goods and monetary penalties on conviction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ; Te Pūtea Matua) is the central bank and the sole prudential regulator of registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021. New Zealand abolished exchange controls in 1984; the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act 1982 remains formally on the statute book but is operationally dormant. RBNZ operates the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS), manages official foreign reserves, and jointly with the Financial Markets Authority supervises payment system clearing and financial-market conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations and maintains a fully convertible, freely floating NZD. Both current-account flows (trade in goods, cross-border e-commerce sales, royalties, agent commissions) and capital-account flows (equity subscriptions, shareholder loans, dividend distributions, loan repayments) are unrestricted and require no RBNZ or Government approval. Profit remittance is unrestricted at the FX level; the only fiscal frictions are non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) and the approved issuer levy (AIL) on interest, dividends and royalties, together with NZ thin-capitalisation and transfer-pricing rules where the entity is treated as an NZ tax resident. For a tax-exempt offshore International Company (CK_IC), no New Zealand permanent establishment must be maintained, and the treasury function should be executed strictly through the exempt entity's bank accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: New Zealand imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory term for repatriation of foreign receipts. An exporter may invoice, receive and hold NZD, USD, CNY or any freely convertible currency. The CK_IC must, however, preserve the full export documentation file (commercial invoices, packing lists, airway bills or bills of lading, shipping certificates and Stripe/Shopify settlement statements) to satisfy both bank AML/CFT due diligence and Statistics New Zealand's overseas merchandise trade reporting. Where export proceeds are retained offshore, no NZ taxable income arises if the entity maintains its non-resident status and no permanent establishment is established.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High as a secondary disbursement and collection rail, Low as the primary treasury rail. New Zealand has no dedicated EMI licensing category; non-bank electronic money institutions and offshore digital EMIs operate under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008 and the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, typically as registered money remitters or payment facilitators. An offshore EMI (for example, Airwallex, Wise or Payoneer-style platforms) can support merchant payout collection from Stripe and Shopify Payments and provide FX conversion, but it cannot access RBNZ ESAS settlement, cannot issue letters of credit or handle documentary collections, and may be rejected as an end-beneficiary bank by NZ tier-1 banks if the EMI has no NZ FSP registration and no group-level correspondent arrangement. Treasury-grade clearing should therefore use a registered NZ bank account as the master settlement account, sweeping EMI balances daily.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is lawful under the AML/CFT Act 2009; physical branch attendance is not a statutory requirement. NZ tier-1 banks, when onboarding a non-resident-owned tax-exempt International Company, typically require (i) certified true or notarised copies of the certificate of incorporation, certificate of incumbency, constitution, registered office particulars and company extract; (ii) a live video-verification interview (Microsoft Teams or Zoom) with each director, shareholder and beneficial owner conducted by the compliance team; (iii) notarised passport and proof-of-address documents for the beneficial owners; and (iv) an original board resolution approving the account and appointed signatories. Physical presence at a New Zealand branch or at an overseas NZ embassy or consulate may be demanded only in enhanced-CDD cases involving FATF-flagged jurisdictions, politically exposed persons, or inconsistent source-of-wealth documentation. To expedite the escrow account, the CK_IC may appoint an NZ-resident non-executive director or a licensed corporate trustee as co-signatory, which satisfies the banks' expectation of a local actor without waiving the non-resident beneficial ownership structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-layer ownership with unidentifiable ultimate beneficial owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A certified ownership chain from the registered agent: certificate of incorporation, certificate of incumbency, full register of members for the International Company, trust deed and trustee resolution where shares are held by an offshore trust, beneficial-owner passports and proof-of-address, and a signed source-of-wealth declaration for each natural person above the 25 per cent threshold.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt status interpreted as the absence of economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A formal written offshore tax opinion from the IC's incorporation counsel confirming exemption and non-resident status, the IRD certificate of non-residence or its equivalent, a contemporaneous economic-substance file comprising lease agreement, director engagement letters, board minutes, procurement and retail contracts, and an arm's-length transfer-pricing policy evidencing that all retail activity is delegated at commercial terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border wires to suppliers or customer refund platforms in higher-risk countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The bank's CDD team is supplied with the annual supplier KYC package (business licence, bank letter confirming account title, beneficial-owner details for each supplier), each shipment's commercial invoices and bill-of-lading or airway-bill matching the Shopify and Stripe settlement reports, a board-approved treasury policy setting maximum per-transaction limits and permitted jurisdictions, and monthly reconciliation statements tracing receipts to disbursements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-list or politically exposed persons screening hits on counterparties or beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The defence pack includes a screening report from a reputable risk-data provider, an explanatory narrative, an independent politically exposed persons declaration under the AML/CFT Act 2009, a transparent chain-of-funds evidence package covering the initial subscription capital, legal counsel sign-off confirming no direct nexus with the listed person, and an agreed structure of ongoing transaction monitoring for 24 months.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital must be injected through the RBNZ-regulated banking channel using the SWIFT MT103 and, where an upstream cover is required, MT202 COV. The remittance must be coded as direct investment or equity, not as goods or services, with the purpose narrative 'Capital Subscription - CK_IC Board Resolution [date]'; miscoding causes false-positive sanctions reviews and may freeze the escrow account for investigation. The beneficiary account during escrow must be named exactly as the CK_IC corporate account, and the bank will apply a holding period, typically 24 to 72 hours, pending completion of enhanced CDD on the remitter. Verification items include a certified copy of the subscription agreement, board or trustee resolution, registered-agent incumbency certificate, and the ultimate origin of funds supported by a source-of-wealth statement. For an exempt-zone CK_IC relying on a New Zealand banking corridor, funds should be routed via a single clean correspondent, for example the bank's New York or Sydney affiliate, and never split into multiple same-day round-number wires, which would trigger structuring alerts under the AML/CFT Act framework.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and logistics payments for the smart-home IoT retail model are cleared over four rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for open-account, proforma-invoice and advance-payment settlements; (ii) commercial letters of credit issued under UCP600, using the MT700 and MT707 message series, for high-value, time-critical procurement requiring shipping-title protection; (iii) documentary collections, D/P or D/A, for repeat mid-value purchase orders; and (iv) merchant-acquirer settlement from Stripe and Shopify Payments, organised first to the operational NZD account and then swept for FX conversion and supplier payment. NZD domestic payments run through the Payments NZ ISO 20022 clearing rails, formerly the Bulk Electronic Clearing System, while FX payments settle via the New York CHIPS and FedWire systems for USD, the Hong Kong CHATS and CNH clearing rails for yuan-leg payments, and SWIFT for all other currencies. Payments must disclose genuine commercial purpose codes with invoice numbers, and each disbursement file should map to the monthly procurement ledger to prevent the bank from reclassifying operational trade payments as capital outflows.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable forward FX contracts (NZD/USD, NZD/CNY, NZD/EUR) up to a 24-month tenor with a registered NZ bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or the bank's standard FX derivatives terms; permitted only for hedging identified commercial receivables and payables, never for speculative open positions.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) over CNY or other restricted currencies where physical delivery of the offshore currency is unavailable; settled in NZD/USD against an agreed fixing rate, for example the CNH offshore rate, and permitted only when a confirmed supplier invoice or firm purchase commitment underlies the hedge.

Cross-currency swaps (NZD/USD) used to align long-term shareholder capital or intercompany funding currency with the operational NZD/USD mix of the retail treasury; documented with a Credit Support Annex for margin posting and subject to RBNZ non-bank counterparty eligibility requirements.

European-style FX options and zero-cost collars on NZD/USD, traded only with a licensed bank or an authorised FMA-regulated broker, to protect tender-offer pricing and seasonal procurement pipelines while preserving upside benefit; each transaction must be recorded under the board-approved treasury risk policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation + 31 working days; filing month is the incorporation anniversary month.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a default notice; continued non-compliance leads to a removal notice and administrative strike-off. Directors may be prosecuted for non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited Financial Statements (conditional on audit threshold / FMC reporting status)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; filed with the New Zealand Companies Office only if the company is an FMC reporting entity or issuer under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after balance date for a large or non-issuer audited company; issuer deadlines apply to FMC reporting entities.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors in default may be prosecuted, fines may be imposed, and the Registrar may require rectification; issuer-related non-filing may also trigger FMA actions.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% (Income Tax Act 2007, Sch 1, Part A, Table 1, company rate for the 2025-26 income year)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays in New Zealand. General incentives only: 15% refundable R&D tax credit (s LY 1), full imputation credit system (effective tax on distributed profits 28%), and non-resident companies taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income (s BD 1(5)). The 'International Company' / 'Tax-Exempt Zone' classification referenced in the entity key is not a standalone New Zealand statutory tax regime; a NZ-incorporated company is resident and taxed on worldwide income at 28% unless treaty tie-breaker rules place residence offshore.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory carryforward period; subject to 49% shareholder continuity under s IA 5 or the business continuity test under s IA 6)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return), filed via Inland Revenue's myIR electronic portal or through approved digital filing software (Xero, MYOB, etc.); paper filing accepted only in limited circumstances.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (income year aligned to the company's balance date; standard balance date is 31 March). No quarterly income tax return is required, but provisional tax is paid in instalments: 28 August, 15 January, and 7 May for a 31 March balance date.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date: IR4 must be filed by 7 July following the income year-end for non-tax-agent companies, or by 31 March following the income year-end for companies utilising an extended tax-agent arrangement. Terminal tax is due 7 April (standard) or 7 February (tax-agent extension). Non-standard balance dates require Commissioner approval and shift all deadlines proportionally.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income from business or trade: retail turnover from smart-home IoT hardware sales (ISIC 4791), excluding GST.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only turnover attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment (PE); offshore e-commerce sales not attributable to the NZ PE must be excluded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income: all taxable interest derived from New Zealand sources and foreign interest if the company is NZ-resident.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies include only New Zealand-sourced interest (s BD 1(5) ITA 2007); gross amounts before NRWT deduction are reportable, with NRWT claimed as a credit in Box 13.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends: gross dividends received plus attached imputation credits and resident withholding tax (RWT).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include NZ-sourced dividends only; fully imputed dividends paid to non-residents are excluded from income when no supplementary dividend is paid, but must still be disclosed in the dividend schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other income: gains on disposal of business assets, foreign exchange gains, insurance settlements, and miscellaneous assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude income not sourced in New Zealand; include income attributable to the NZ PE, net of allowable expenditure (s DA 1).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income: arithmetic sum of Boxes 1, 2, 3 and 4.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that total income equals only the NZ-sourced assessable income of the PE; do not include loan proceeds or capital contributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Purchases and cost of goods sold: acquisition cost of IoT devices, imported hardware components, freight, customs duty and direct product costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attribute cost of goods sold to the NZ PE on an arm's-length transfer pricing basis; intercompany purchases from the foreign head office must reflect comparable uncontrolled prices (s GC 13).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Wages and salaries: remuneration of NZ employees, including employer superannuation and fringe benefit tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only wages of employees physically working for the NZ PE and on the NZ payroll are deductible; head-office recharge of foreign staff costs must satisfy transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Other deductible expenses: rent, marketing, software subscriptions, platform transaction fees (Stripe/Shopify Payments), insurance, professional fees, depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apportion shared costs on an arm's-length basis to the NZ PE; non-deductible head-office charges and royalties that lack economic substance must be excluded (s DA 1(2)).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit before tax (or net loss before tax): trading result after all adjustments for non-deductible expenditure and transfer pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must be computed solely from NZ PE activity; overseas losses are not deductible against NZ income unless the loss offset provisions of Part I apply to a resident company.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: net profit less loss carry-forwards applied in the current year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident companies, taxable income cannot exceed the net NZ-sourced income amount; treaty protection under the PE article must be separately evidenced.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax on taxable income: apply the 28% company rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 28% only to the taxable income attributable to the NZ PE; no lower rate is available to non-resident companies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: RWT, FWT, imputation credits, foreign tax credits, PAyE and supplementary dividend credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim NRWT withheld at source on NZ interest/dividends, and foreign tax credits only where a NZ DTA or domestic unilateral relief provision confers entitlement (s LJ/LK).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual tax payable or refund due: final balance payable to the Commissioner or refundable to the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refunds to non-resident companies are not issued unless all returns are filed, the company holds the required certificates (IR291), and the refund does not breach the DTA refund rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty NZ$250 per IR4 (reduced to NZ$50 if all tax is paid by the statutory due date and the return is merely late); late payment penalty 1% immediately on the first day of default plus an additional 4% on the eighth day, then 1% per month on the outstanding balance; use-of-money interest (UOMI) at the prescribed company debit rate (approximately 8.4% p.a. for the 2025-26 year) compounds daily. The Commissioner may also impose a NZ$250 electronic filing penalty for failing to file via myIR when required.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on gross dividends paid to non-resident shareholders (s RF 8 and Sch 1, Part A, Table 4, Income Tax Act 2007). Fully imputed dividends attract no NRWT, but any supplementary dividend paid to gross up the imputed distribution brings the combined effective rate to 30%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Step 1: confirm treaty residence of the recipient under Article 4 of the applicable Double Taxation Agreement (DTA), including any tie-breaker analysis. Step 2: obtain a Certificate of Residence (TRC/CoR) from the foreign revenue authority. Step 3: deliver the TRC and completed Inland Revenue declaration form IR290 (one-off) or IR291 (continuous certificate) to the New Zealand payer before payment; the payer then applies the reduced treaty rate at source. Step 4: where the statutory 30% was withheld, the non-resident must file an IR3NR/IR4NR return and attach the TRC and IR291 to claim the refund of any excess NRWT. Reduced treaty rates typically follow the OECD pattern: 15% portfolio dividends, 5% for a 10%+ corporate shareholding, 10% interest, 10% royalties, subject to the relevant treaty text and any limitation-of-benefits provision.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory NRWT 15%; most New Zealand DTAs reduce withholding to 10%; alternatively, the 2% Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) under s 86I of the Stamp and Cheques Duties Act 1971 applies to qualifying registered securities and fully replaces NRWT. Royalties for IP (patents, trademarks, know-how, software) and industrial/technical equipment: statutory NRWT 15%; most DTAs reduce to 10% (certain treaties provide 5% for equipment royalties). The source rules for interest (s RF 9) and royalties (s RF 10) turn on the residence of the payer and the PE to which the payment is attributable.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: From income years commencing on or after 1 April 2025, mandatory transfer pricing documentation (Master File and Local File) is required where the New Zealand group has annual turnover of NZ$100 million or more and the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions is NZ$10 million or more. Below these thresholds, contemporaneous TP documentation is not statutorily mandatory, but the Commissioner may request it at any time and the 30-day production rule applies (s GC 13, Tax Administration Act 1994).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not operate Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations. Substance is nonetheless enforced through: (i) the general anti-avoidance rule (s BG 1), which voids arrangements with a dominant tax-avoidance purpose; (ii) PE attribution rules (s GB 1 and DTA Article 7), which impute profits to any New Zealand fixed place of business; (iii) the 2025 mandatory TP documentation regime requiring an explicit functional, risk and capital analysis; and (iv) judicial anti-shell principles that may disregard an interposed tax-exempt 'International Company' with no employees, premises, or risk-bearing capacity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting New Zealand-sourced retail income from IoT hardware sales from the IR4, overstating deductible expenses, manufacturing fake R&D tax credit claims, or concealing a taxable PE through offshore invoicing structures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Prosecution under s 143B Tax Administration Act 1994: imprisonment up to 5 years and/or a fine of NZ$50,000 per offence; civil shortfall penalty up to 150% of the evaded tax plus late payment penalties and UOMI; dishonest-use-of-document offences under s 228 Crimes Act 1961 can result in up to 7 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be jointly and severally liable under s 149 TAA for unremitted PAYE/RWT, liable for reckless trading under s 135 Companies Act 1993, and criminally liable for fraudulent trading under s 380 Companies Act 1993 (imprisonment up to 5 years and/or fine up to NZ$200,000). Departure prohibition orders and asset restraint orders under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009 are available where tax debts exceed NZ$10,000.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the 'Tax-Exempt Zone' International Company as a booking vehicle that holds the retail revenue contracts, IP or treasury functions without offices, employees, operational risk, or real decision-making in the claimed tax jurisdiction, while the actual IoT hardware retail business is managed and executed in New Zealand.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The arrangement may be voided under s BG 1; the Commissioner may reattribute the income to the NZ operating company or PE; shortfall penalties of 50% (unacceptable tax position) or 100% (abusive tax position) plus UOMI apply; the foreign parent may be assessed directly as having a New Zealand PE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be disqualified under s 298 Companies Act 1993 for up to 5 years; personal liability for unpaid company tax may arise under the director penalty regime; travel bans under s 27 TAA can be imposed on directors with significant tax debts; criminal exposure exists for officers who sign false declarations in the IR4.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as an unregistered financial service business by moving beyond pure goods retail into stored-value facilities, wallet issuance, remittance services, or virtual-asset (crypto/IoT token) payment processing, without registering and supervising under the AML/CFT Act 2009 and the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Dispute Resolution) Act 2008.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML/CFT Act 2009 civil penalties of up to NZ$2,000,000 for a company (s 90(3)) and up to NZ$300,000 per officer or manager; criminal penalties of up to NZ$2,000,000 or three times the benefit derived; the FMA or DIA may publish enforcement actions and suspend or prohibit the business.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and senior managers are personally liable for the company's unpaid AML penalty if the company cannot pay (s 90(4) AML/CFT Act); breach of the FSP Act while unregistered exposes each director to fines of up to NZ$100,000 per offence and banning orders from managing financial services.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Thin Capitalisation Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare and retain contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation where the NZ group exceeds NZ$100 million turnover and NZ$10 million related-party dealings; underpricing IoT hardware imports from a foreign affiliate, paying excessive head-office royalties, or using non-arm's-length intra-group guarantees to create artificial deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalties up to 50% of the resulting tax shortfall for an unacceptable tax position, up to 100% for an abusive tax position, plus UOMI; the Commissioner may reconstruct pricing under s GC 13 and deny DTA relief where the recipient lacks substance; thin capitalisation adjustments can disallow interest deductions above the 60% debt-to-asset safe harbour in foreign-controlled New Zealand companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly cause or allow a false or misleading transfer pricing position may be assessed personally for penalties under s 149 TAA, subject to disqualification under s 298 Companies Act 1993, and, where deliberate mispricing defrauds creditors, prosecuted for fraudulent trading under s 380 Companies Act 1993 with potential imprisonment of up to 5 years.
